newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive to review dividend policy.
newsitem.headline: Incentive to review dividend policy.

text.p: Swedish holding company Incentive AB said on Thursday it would review its dividend policy and would introduce an options programme for about 50 senior executives.

"In order to more effectively meet the demands imposed on a growth company, the board has also decided to review the principles governing the payment of dividends," Incentive head Mikael Lilius told the annual general shareholders' meeting.
The allocation of options will be based on the value that is created in the company, he said.
"Creating value requires that operations be focused on satisfying customers' needs and ensuring that the company functions in a responsible manner in the society," Lilius said.

"The shareholders perspective is important in particular because investors and financial investors are increasingly changing over to evaluating companies based on discounted cash flows rather than on traditional price/earnings ratio."
Incentive said it was counting on growth in its medical technology subsidiary Gambro of 15 percent a year.
"Ten percent through internal growth and five percent through acquisition," Lilius said.
"During 1996 we invested close to 700 million crowns to acquire and establish dialysis clinics.
"We have ambitious future objectives for Gambro to strengthen its position as one of the leading companies in its industry and grow at a faster rate than the industry."
